title: IPC peer path changed
description: The data of a `peer.path_changed` event (2.1): a peer the connection has a route to -- a direct message exchanged with it, or a broadcast received from it on one of its joins -- changed path, `direct | relayed` either way — or, from IPC 2.4 (1.1.0, A 2026-10-09), the route BEGAN or a routed peer CONNECTED AGAIN after a `peer.disconnected`: `previous` absent, `current` the peer's path at that moment, `reason_class` `route_established` or `reconnected`. Coalesced per peer to one pending: a newer change keeps the pending one's `previous` and takes the newer `current`, `reason_class` and `observed_at`; one whose `previous` equals its `current` is withdrawn. The IPC projection of `LocalSessionEvent::PeerPathChanged` and of TRANSPORT.md's `PeerPathChanged`.

previous.description: The path before the change. ABSENT when the route begins or a routed peer connects again after a `peer.disconnected` (1.1.0, IPC 2.4): the notice then carries the peer's current path; its `reason_class` is `route_established` or `reconnected` when fresh, or a later change's class when such a pending notice was merged with that change (coalescing keeps the absent `previous` and takes the newer `current`, `reason_class` and `observed_at`). A connection below 2.4 is never sent a notice without `previous`.

reason_class.description: Why the path changed: the runtime's reason classes (`direct_established`, `direct_lost`, ...); on a notice without `previous` (1.1.0) `route_established` when the route begins or `reconnected` when a routed peer connects again, or — when that pending notice was merged with a later change — the later change's class.
